Doro.content: DM: Session 1 - the Salt Lantern. The harbour town of Brinemouth hires you: the old lighthouse on Gull Rock went dark three nights ago, and two ships have already wrecked on the reef. You row out at low tide. The lighthouse door hangs open; inside, the spiral stair is crusted with fresh salt, and something wet drags itself around above you. On the ground floor: a keeper's desk with a logbook written in an old coastal script, a locked sea-chest, and a smashed oil lamp. Up the stair you hear a clicking, like claws on stone. What do you do?
I check the logbook for recent entries. That clicking sounds like something big—if we're going up, I'd better Raise a Shield first. [Arcana to decipher the logbook].

DM (results): Doro deciphers the logbook (Society 18): the keeper's last entry reads "The Salt Mother wants her lamp back. I gave her the oil. I will give her the light." Pim spots a brass spyglass wedged behind the desk (Perception 21) and pockets it, but the sea-chest lock beats him (16 vs 18). Ione can't read the rest of the script (15). Buck's flying kick carries him up the spiral stair (Acrobatics 25) - he lands on the landing face to face with a giant crab crusted in salt. Kestrel spotted it first (crit) and puts two arrows in it (3, then a NAT 20 crit for 10). A second salt crab clacks down from above, and at the top of the stair a drowned lighthouse keeper, glowing faintly, is prying the great lens out of the lamp. FIGHT, round 1 (3 actions each in PF2e). What do you do?

I brace myself, ready to intercept the keeper if it tries to descend. "Pim, Kestrel—focus on the crabs. Buck, watch the keeper. Ione, can you do something about the lens?" I Raise a Shield, then Stride to the stair, and Strike at the nearest crab with my warhammer. [Shield Block, Acrobatics for footing, Strike].

DM (results): Doro's warhammer cracks crab A's shell (6) and his raised shield turns its claw. Kestrel adds an arrow (2) - crab A is at half. Pim's dagger skids off crab B, which snaps him hard (13 damage), but he still slips up the stair unseen (Stealth crit) and is now right behind the keeper. Ione's fire ray backfires (NAT 1): the flame puffs in her face and singes Glafka's feathers. Buck snatches the spyglass from Pim (Athletics 21), flashes lamplight into the keeper's eyes and - for once - lands the flying kick (26): the great lens tumbles from the keeper's hands and teeters on the gallery rail. The keeper grabs Buck by the throat; seawater pours from Buck's mouth (drowning). Round 2 (3 actions each). What do you do?

"Pim, get that lens! Kestrel, finish off crab A. Ione, help Buck!" I Shift my Shield to Buck, then Stride past the keeper to strike at crab B. I'll use Demanding Challenge to try to draw its attention. "Crab, you fight me!" [Shield Block, Stride, Demanding Challenge, Strike].

DM (results): Doro's Demanding Challenge pulls crab B onto him; he cracks it (7) and takes a hard claw (11). Pim throws salt in the keeper's eyes (26) - blinding him - and then does exactly what he said: knocks the great lens off the rail (crit). It falls the whole stairwell and SHATTERS on the ground floor. Buck wrenches free of the keeper's grip (26) but his backflip off the rail fails (17) and he lands on his face. Kestrel's crit (18) leaves crab A barely alive; it claws Kestrel (9); Kestrel's shout at the keeper doesn't land. Ione can't make sense of the spyglass (11). With the lens gone the keeper wails "the light, the light is gone" and collapses into a puddle of salt water; the crabs scuttle out a window into the sea. The lighthouse is dark and its lens is broken - Brinemouth will not be happy.
DOWNTIME: three days in Brinemouth while the town argues about the lens. The town has a glassworks, a fish market, a sailors' temple of Gozreh, a tavern with an arm-wrestling table, the harbourmaster (furious), and a scholar who might read the logbook's old script. What does your character spend the three days doing? Give 2-3 things.

First, I'll head to the sailors' temple to make an offering to Gozreh, asking for her guidance on how to deal with the Salt Mother. Then, I'll track down that scholar to get a proper translation of the logbook—maybe there's more to it than we realized. Finally, I'll hit the tavern to see if any of the locals know about the Salt Mother and her lamp. If I'm lucky, I might even find a sparring partner for some arm-wrestling. [Religion to learn about Gozreh, Society to find the scholar, Athletics for arm-wrestling].
